messages:
jess: :loudspeaker: Heads-up: we're rolling out a new SDK + docs policy to require explicit model_pin and runtime_weight defaults in our public examples. Goal: avoid silent behavior changes when model variants or runtime heuristics update. TL;DR: docs and SDK defaults change next week, see checklist below.

kumar: sounds sensible. what's the timeline?

jess: calendar: we plan a staged rollout starting 2026-04-01. Stage 1 (docs + examples): publish new samples and a migration guide on 04/01. Stage 2 (SDK defaults): 04/08 SDK minor release flips default from `auto` -> `stable` for model selection; SDK will log a one-time notice. Stage 3 (enforcement): 05/01 telemetry warns on missing model_pin in production configs.

ran: @jess does this affect any security or compliance controls (KMS/HSM integrations or telemetry)?

jess: @ran short answer: no KMS impact. telemetry change is a diagnostic flag only. We'll add an audit field in request logs for model_pin/runtime_weight. ops-bot will surface aggregated counts to eng-sre.

marie: can we get a devex runbook for customers who relied on `auto`? We need copy for sales & CSMs.

jess: yes — docs-bot will publish a migration guide and templated customer email. Key migration points: explain why pinning improves stability, provide quick CLI snippet, and give rollback instructions.

docs-bot: Published draft: https://go.redwood/docs/pin-policy-draft (internal only). Migration snippet: ```json
{
  "model_pin": "redwood/claim-stable-1.0",
  "runtime_weight": "balanced"
}
```

kumar: for the SDK change, will there be a compatibility shim? some apps read config from env vars `REDWOOD_MODEL` etc.

jess: we'll add SDK logging that detects env var usage and emits a migration hint. No hard-breaking behavior — default changes are opt-out until 05/01.

tom: can eng-platform add an automated migrator that suggests pins based on production traffic? would help a lot.

kumar: +1 to that. we can run an offline job that samples requests and suggests the best stable() candidate. I'll sketch a PR.

ran: what about release notes checklist for security review?

jess: checklist (short):
- update docs examples and quickstart (docs-bot)
- publish migration guide and customer FAQ (docs + product)
- SDK minor release with notice + env-var shim (eng-sdk)
- telemetry schema update and internal dashboard (eng-sre)
- inform sales/CS and legal for contract language if needed (go-to-market)
- schedule Q&A drop-in 2026-03-30 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent)

marie: can we add a default 'recommended pin' field in docs examples to make it easy for users to copy/paste?

jess: yes — every example will include a `recommended_pin` comment and a short rationale sentence.

kumar: I'll put a tiny migration CLI in the SDK repo: `rw migrate-pins --suggest --apply` — will push a WIP branch today.

docs-bot: FYI: legal reviewed the draft copy, no contract changes required for now.

ran: noted. i'll add an audit entry to our tracing spec so model_pin appears in traces.

tom: small question: runtime_weight values allowed? balanced|latency|cost|throughput ?

jess: allowed set = [balanced, latency, cost, throughput, conservative]. We'll document recommended mappings.

kumar: pushed draft PR for CLI migrator: https://go.redwood/pull/1221. Needs review from eng-platform and docs.

marie: thanks all. Sales asked for a short blurb we can use in outreach. draft here: "We now recommend pinning a stable model variant in production to avoid silent quality regressions; see migration guide." Thoughts?

jess: good. add one sentence about how runtime_weight can reduce bill by ~10-30% for some workloads.

ops-bot: Reminder: Q&A drop-in today 2026-03-30 10:00 PT (Zoom link posted in calendar).

kumar: Reviewed comments from eng-platform. I'll coordinate the rollout windows to avoid coincide with infra maintenance.

ran: LGTM from security.

jess: thanks team — action owners: @kumar (SDK migrator + release), @docs-bot (migration guide + examples), @eng-platform (suggestion job), @marie (CS/sales copy), @ran (trace + audit). If anyone sees blockers, reply here or join the Q&A. :rocket:
